outcome: Complications (bladder injury, wound infection, postoperative fever)
cohort: 40 pregnant women with previous cesarean deliveries and diagnosed with placenta previa and/or placenta accreta
finding: Using the cervix as a natural tamponade was successful in stopping bleeding in 95% of the cases (38 out of 40 patients) with placenta previa and/or placenta accreta, suggesting it as a safe, simple, time-saving, and potentially effective method for controlling severe postpartum hemorrhage.
